questions.question: You’re waiting in line at the café when your friend’s order is served before yours. What would be the most polite way to apologise?
options: Don’t worry about it! It happens all the time.
I’m sorry, but I’m next—could you take this for me?
You’re lucky! I’ll just get mine after you.
It’s not your fault; the system is just slow today.
questions.answer: I’m sorry, but I’m next—could you take this for me?

questions.question: Your colleague asks, ‘Do you think we should move the meeting to 3 PM instead of 4?’ What would be the most appropriate response if you agree but want to suggest a specific time?
options: Yes, let’s do it! 3 PM is fine with me.
I don’t think 3 PM is good—what about 2 PM?
No, 4 PM is better—it’s when everyone is free.
That’s a good idea, but maybe 3:15 would work better.
questions.answer: Yes, let’s do it! 3 PM is fine with me.

questions.question: Your friend says, ‘I really enjoyed the concert last night!’ How would you politely respond if you had mixed feelings?
options: That’s great! I’m glad you liked it.
I’m not sure I agree—I found it a bit confusing.
It was okay, but the band could have played slower.
I think you should have gone with someone else.
questions.answer: I’m not sure I agree—I found it a bit confusing.

questions.question: You’re at a formal dinner and the host asks, ‘Would you like another glass of wine?’ What would be the most appropriate response?
options: No, thank you—I’ve had enough.
Yes, please! I’d love another one.
I’m not sure—I’ll think about it.
I don’t drink wine, but I’ll have water instead.

questions.question: Your neighbour asks, ‘Can you help me move my sofa? It’s heavy!’ What would be the best way to politely offer help?
options: No, I’m sorry—I can’t help with that.
Of course! I’d be happy to give you a hand.
That’s a lot of work—maybe someone else can do it.
I’ll think about it—I might be able to help later.
questions.answer: Of course! I’d be happy to give you a hand.
